samples.summary: New copy-refusal for deeply nested tables has no test at all
samples.evidence: `DocumentCopyService` now throws `BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: …')` when `documentHasTableAtNestingCap(content)` (document-copy.service.ts:446-451). Grepping the whole repo for `Cannot copy this document`, `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` and `nesting` finds no hit in `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts` or any other spec. So neither direction is pinned: a false positive (an ordinary document refused, i.e. copy suddenly 400s for users) nor a regression that removes the guard (a copy that silently drops truncated rows — the data loss the guard exists to prevent) would fail CI. The only coverage of the predicate is indirect, via `writeDocsRoot` in docs-tree.spec.ts, which exercises a different call path.

samples.summary: Controller depth-cap change (`> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` → `>= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) has no boundary test; existing tests pass either way
samples.evidence: docs-content.validation.spec.ts only covers depth 2 ('still accepts the nesting a real document reaches', lines 104-112) and OVERFLOW_DEPTH = 20000 (lines 82-102). Both constants are 32, so a body nested exactly 32 deep — the one input whose classification this hunk changes (was accepted then 500'd by the writer, now a 400) — is asserted nowhere, and neither is 31-accepted. Reverting the hunk to the old comparison leaves the suite green.

samples.summary: Editor-level `insertTable` nesting refusal (early return before the split) is untested
samples.evidence: editor.ts:4228-4234 adds an early `return` when `doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, whose stated point is that the command declines *before* `doc.splitBlock`, so no stray empty paragraph is left and the model-level throw at document.ts:925 is never surfaced to the user. Only the model-level throw is tested (table-nesting.test.ts:156-159 `insertTableInCell refuses to nest past the cap`). No test drives `editor.insertTable`/the Insert Table command with a caret at the cap; grepping packages/docs/test/view for `insertTable` finds only tables inserted at ordinary depths.

samples.summary: Paste-time nesting cap is only unit-tested on the helper; the wiring in `insertBlocks` is untested
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` now computes `capTableNesting(incoming, this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId))` (text-editor.ts:4562-4572) and bails when the result is empty. Tests cover `capTableNesting` directly with a hand-supplied `baseDepth` (table-nesting.test.ts:161-201) but nothing exercises a paste through the editor into a deep cell, so passing the wrong base depth (e.g. 0, or the table's depth instead of the caret's) — which would silently write past the cap or silently drop pasted tables — is not caught. Also untested: the new `if (blocks.length === 0) return` early exit, which changes what a paste of only over-deep tables does.

samples.summary: Backend writeDocsRoot cap: accepted-boundary case is one level short, and the footer arm of `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` is untested
samples.evidence: The new suite accepts `nested(MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH - 1)` and refuses `nested(MAX + 1)` (docs-tree.spec.ts:731-756). The true accepted boundary is `nested(MAX)` (tables at depths 0…MAX-1), which is never written — an off-by-one that refused legitimate documents at exactly the cap would keep the suite green (the frontend suite does pin this case, the backend one does not). `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` also checks `document.footer` (docs-tree.ts:254); only the body and header arms have tests.

samples.summary: Backend `buildBlockNode`'s `depth >= cap → no rows` branch is unreachable from any test (writeDocsRoot refuses first)
samples.evidence: `writeDocsRoot` throws on `documentHasTableAtNestingCap(document)` (docs-tree.ts:376) before calling `buildTreeChildren`, and `buildBlockNode` is reachable only through that path in this file, so the empty-rows branch at docs-tree.ts:177-181 can never be exercised by a test and none attempts it. Compare the frontend store, where the same branch *is* reachable through the incremental writers and is pinned. Untested-and-unreachable code here means a future caller that bypasses `writeDocsRoot` gets no protection the suite can vouch for.

samples.summary: Layout cap test only asserts 'does not throw'; the stated placeholder-line invariant is unasserted
samples.evidence: `layoutCellBlocks` now pushes one empty line past the cap specifically so the cell's `lines`/`blockBoundaries` stay in step with its blocks ('every caret and hit-test index depends on that correspondence', table-layout.ts:135-145). The only test — table-nesting.test.ts 'lays out a chain deep enough to overflow the stack' — asserts `.not.toThrow()` and nothing else, so a version that `continue`d without pushing the placeholder (desynchronising caret/hit-test indices, a silently wrong caret for users) passes identically.

samples.summary: Only two of the incremental writers' depth plumbing is pinned; insertBlocksAfter, insertTableRow, insertTableColumn and splitBlock are not
samples.evidence: The new frontend tests cover `insertBlockAfter` (at and one under the cap) and `updateTableCell`. `insertBlocksAfter` (siblingDepth), `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn` (the new `resolveTableRowDepth`, rowDepth = pathDepth + 1) and `splitBlock` (blockDepth) all received depth arguments in this diff with no test asserting the depth they pass, so an off-by-one in `resolveTableRowDepth` — writing rows/cells one level past the cap, i.e. CRDT content no reader materializes — would ship green. `insertBlocksAfter` is the path a multi-block paste takes.
searchedFor: read the yorkie-doc-store.test.ts hunk in the diff

samples.summary: The snapshot adapter's own nesting cap cannot fail its tests — `docsTreeToDocument` caps the same chain
samples.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode`'s new row-depth cap is asserted only through `parseDocsSnapshot` (snapshot-adapters.test.ts, 'stops descending at the cap…'), which then runs `docsTreeToDocument` — itself capped at the same constant. Removing the adapter's cap entirely leaves both assertions (`blocks[0].type === 'table'`, chain length === cap) true, as the test's own comment concedes ('Isolating the adapter's own cap is not possible from out here by design'). The new recursion bound in this file is therefore effectively uncovered; its failure mode (stack overflow while normalizing a hostile snapshot) is contained only because the parser currently gives out first.

samples.summary: New defensive clamps/guards with no test: buildCellRangeRects layout clamp, range-slices widest-row fold, findOuterCellAddress cycle guard
samples.evidence: Three hardening changes in this diff have no test I can find: (a) `buildCellRangeRects` now clamps to `tl.cells.length`/`tl.columnXOffsets.length` (selection.ts:788-799) — the tests only exercise rectangles that `normalizeCellRange` already clamped, so the fallback bound is never the thing under test; (b) `visitCellRectangleSlices`'s spread→reduce change (range-slices.ts:56-58) has no test with a row count near the spread limit nor an equivalence test; (c) `TextEditor.findOuterCellAddress`'s new `seen` cycle guard (text-editor.ts:3894-3904) — the cyclic-map tests cover `moveToNextCell`/`moveToPrevCell`, `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `resolvePositionPixel`, `normalizeRange` and `Doc.findBlock`, but not this walk.

samples.summary: Filler assertions in the Shift+Tab cycle test
samples.evidence: `expect(leafId).toBeDefined()` is true regardless of the guard (it is a local id built by the fixture), and `expect(typeof editor._getCursorForTest().blockId).toBe('string')` holds for any caret. The load-bearing assertion is `expect(press(container, 'Tab', true)).toBeUndefined()`; the other two add no signal and read as coverage that is not there.

finding.summary: New copy-refusal for deeply nested tables has no test at all
finding.evidence: `DocumentCopyService` now throws `BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: …')` when `documentHasTableAtNestingCap(content)` (document-copy.service.ts:446-451). Grepping the whole repo for `Cannot copy this document`, `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` and `nesting` finds no hit in `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts` or any other spec. So neither direction is pinned: a false positive (an ordinary document refused, i.e. copy suddenly 400s for users) nor a regression that removes the guard (a copy that silently drops truncated rows — the data loss the guard exists to prevent) would fail CI. The only coverage of the predicate is indirect, via `writeDocsRoot` in docs-tree.spec.ts, which exercises a different call path.

verdict.reason: The refusal at document-copy.service.ts:446-451 (BadRequestException for documentHasTableAtNestingCap) has no test in any spec or e2e suite. document-copy.service.spec.ts's only doc-arm test (line 219) copies a single paragraph block; its BadRequestException cases cover image-rehost policy and unsupported type. The e2e document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts has no table content at all, and documents.controller.spec.ts mocks DocumentCopyService.copy outright. Decisively, `tableData` — needed to build any nested-table fixture — occurs in only 5 backend files (docs-tree.ts/spec, docs-content.controller.ts and its two specs), none of them on the copy path, so no backend test can construct a document that reaches this guard. The only nesting-cap coverage is docs-tree.spec.ts:711-758 over writeDocsRoot's own `/nested at or past/` throw, a different function and message that would not fail if the copy-side check were removed (silent row loss on copy) or fired wrongly (ordinary copies 400ing). Major under the test-adequacy rubric: an untested guard whose failure either loses document data or breaks a user-visible copy path.

finding.summary: New depth cap in `normalizeYsonTreeNode` has no test at all
finding.evidence: This delta adds a `row`-counting depth cap to `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (snapshot-adapters.ts, the `if (!(isRow && depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH))` branch), justified by "a peer-written block > row > cell > block > table > … chain overflows the stack on this recursion before the capped reader ever sees it". No test exercises it: `packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts` has no reference to MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH or to any deeply nested tree (its deepest cases are the fixture table and the 4-level 'YSON parse limits' tree at line 362). A grep for MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across the repo returns only yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, docx-importer.test.ts and table-nesting.test.ts — no history test. So neither the stack-overflow protection nor the off-by-one of counting `row` ancestors (whether this walk truncates at the same table `docsTreeToDocument` does) is pinned; a regression would only show as a crashed revision-preview tab or a silently different truncation.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual premise is false. `packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts` imports MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH at line 11 and contains a dedicated `describe('the revision-preview table-nesting cap')` block at lines 392-447 that directly exercises the new cap. It builds arbitrarily deep snapshot-dialect `block > row > cell > block > table` chains via `nestedTables()` (lines 399-413) — the exact peer-written shape the cap guards — and asserts through the real, unmocked `parseDocsSnapshot` (imported line 16, the caller of `normalizeYsonTreeNode`). Both boundary directions are pinned non-vacuously: a chain at cap-1 must read in full (lines 429-432, fails if the walk truncates early) and a 200-level chain must still open as a table and truncate to exactly MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (lines 434-446, fails if the cap is removed — an uncapped walk yields 200 — or is off by one). This defeats both halves of the finding: the stack-overflow/truncation behavior and the off-by-one of counting `row` ancestors. The residual nuance — that the test cannot isolate this adapter's cap from `docsTreeToDocument`'s cap — is acknowledged deliberately at snapshot-adapters.ts:135-140 and in the test header at lines 383-390, and amounts to coverage narrower than ideal, not the claimed absence of any test.

finding.summary: New cycle guards in moveToNextCell/moveToPrevCell are untested
finding.evidence: The delta adds a `seen` set to `moveToNextCell`/`moveToPrevCell` so a cyclic peer-written `blockParentMap` (A → B → A) stops the walk instead of recursing until the stack blows on Tab / Shift-Tab. No test drives a Tab press over a cyclic parent map: only two test files dispatch a 'Tab' key (`test/view/header-table-nav.test.ts`, `test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts`), and neither builds a cyclic map; the existing cycle tests in `test/view/nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:334-422` cover `normalizeRange`, `Doc.findBlock` and `resolvePositionPixel` but not the editor's cell navigation. Comparable guards on this PR did get tests, so this one is an unpinned guard whose failure mode is a hard tab crash for every peer of a malformed document.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file for exactly this guard exists: packages/docs/test/view/cell-nav-cycle.test.ts. It builds a genuinely cyclic blockParentMap by reusing block id 'T1' across an outer and inner table (:75-81), pins that the map loops T1→T2→T1 (:135-141), then dispatches a real Shift+Tab keydown on the editor textarea (:143-153), which routes through text-editor.ts:1185-1187 → handleTab(true) (:2726-2734) → moveToPrevCell() and its seen/visited guard (:6046,6089-6093). The assertion is non-vacuous: press() (:115-133) installs a window 'error' listener precisely because jsdom converts listener exceptions into error events, so an unguarded RangeError stack overflow would be captured and fail expect(...).toBeUndefined(). A second test (:169-199) covers the forward walk moveToNextCell via ArrowRight (text-editor.ts:3088, guard at :6025-6029) by instrumenting doc.getBlock and asserting a bounded lookup count (<100; 18 guarded vs ~12,282 unguarded) — a real discriminator, since handleArrow's catch would otherwise hide the overflow. The file is picked up by the default vitest include (packages/docs/package.json:36, no custom vitest config) and contains no .skip/.only. The finding's central claim that only header-table-nav.test.ts and editor-tab-bullet.test.ts dispatch a 'Tab' key, and that no test drives Tab over a cyclic parent map, is false for this working tree.
